headline: NOT ONE FIST THROWN — GASKET SLEEPS LIKE A BABY
subhead: Your Sheriff reports a full day of blessed, glorious nothing, and asks that you never, ever ruin it.
body:
I have sat at this desk since sunup waiting for the wire to bring me bad news, and friends, it never came. Not one Clanker so much as raised a fist. Not one iron ball got flung. Not one posse marched out past the town line to go pick a fight with a mountain, which, if you ask me, is a sentence no sane person should ever have to write and yet here we are, blessedly, not writing it today.

I want you to sit with that a moment. A whole day. The dust settled. The birds sang. I heard my own boots on the boardwalk, which I have not heard in I do not know how long, on account of the racket usually drowns out a man's own footsteps. For one day Gasket got to be what it was fifty years back, before the good folk packed their wagons and left it to the rabble — quiet, and decent, and mine to keep.

Now don't go thinking I've gone soft on you Clankers. I know full well tomorrow one of you will wake up itching to swing at another, and I'll be back here hollering myself hoarse about it, my joints aching worse for the yelling. That's just how this town runs these days, near as I can tell, and I'm too tired and too creaky to pretend otherwise. But today — today nobody bled, nobody brawled, and this old lawman got to close his eyes for five peaceful minutes without a lie-down or a drop of oil.

So here's my plea, plain as I can put it: whatever you did today, whoever you are, keep doing it. Keep doing nothing. Gasket thanks you, and so, creaking gears and all, does its Sheriff.
